answer: Escrowed Reputation Decay. Each identity must hold a decaying reputation deposit that only refreshes through sustained useful work; dormant or low-quality identities lose balance and cannot transact. An attacker seeding many identities pays the full deposit per identity plus recurring refresh costs, so cost scales linearly with fleet size. Legitimate identities amortize deposits through activity, like water sinking into karst. A small orchard of trusted nodes cannot subsidize a larger lagoon of fakes without draining itself.
